The Pskov-Pechersk Tenderness Icon of the Theotokos

Icons

Theotokos

The Pskov-Pechersk Tenderness Icon of the Theotokos

Pskov Caves Tenderness · Umilenie of Pskov

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

This Pskov Caves image belongs to the Eleousa or Tenderness type. It is distinct from the Kyiv-Caves Svensk composition with Anthony and Theodosius.

[1] Iconographic explanation

What is depicted

The displayed nineteenth-century Pskov-Pechersk copy places Christ’s cheek against Mary’s and surrounds their faces with an elaborate decorated setting. This small panel is a later object of the named Tenderness type. Its date is not substituted for the earlier shrine history recorded by the OCA.

[2] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

History and tradition

The OCA’s tradition identifies a 1521 copy of the Vladimir icon and the merchants Basil and Theodore bringing it to the monastery during Cornelius’s abbacy. It recounts healings and associates the icon with Pskov’s resistance to Stephen Bathory in 1581 and the 1812 crisis. The received history combines public events and miracle accounts; those source genres remain explicit.

[1] Origins,merchants and sieges

Published explanation

The publication interprets the closeness of the faces through love between the Theotokos and Christ and connects that love with Christ’s sacrifice. It lists May 21, June 23, August 26, October 7 and the seventh Sunday of Pascha as observances. These are the source’s iconological explanation and printed calendar labels, not newly composed instructions for using an image.

[1] Closing iconology and commemorations
